file: brain/storage.db (TEENY_STORAGE overrides; found as bin/lib/teeny.sh does). OpenHuman's SQLite store, opened read-only by Teeny: file:<path>?mode=ro, 5 s busy timeout. Never written by Teeny.

table.name: docs

columns.id: text, the document id (a job id, or a lease key)
columns.body: text, JSON for the cron collections; other collections keep non-JSON bodies, so every query first narrows with json_valid(body) in a MATERIALIZED CTE

table.ddl_in_tests: create table docs (scope text default '', coll text, id text, created_ms integer default 0, updated_ms integer default 0, deleted integer default 0, body text)

body_fields.name: string, teeny.<name> or mind.<slug> or a core system job
body_fields.enabled: boolean/0/1; absent or null reads as enabled (coalesce(enabled, 1)); bin/crons shows 'no' only when it is 0
body_fields.next_run_ms: integer epoch ms of the next run
body_fields.schedule: object {kind: 'cron'|'at', expr, tz, at}; selected with json_extract(body, '$.schedule') as JSON text and parsed in Python; '$.schedule.tz' is read directly by bin/crons
body_fields.command: string, shell jobs (read by evolve cron failure evidence)
body_fields.created_ms: integer, preferred over the column when present (catch_up)

cron.runs.filter: coll = 'cron.runs' and deleted = 0 and json_valid(body) and body != '{}'

body_fields.status: string, 'error' marks a failed run (counted); other values include 'ok'
body_fields.finished_ms: integer epoch ms; null/absent while running
body_fields.seq: integer, ordering within a job (row_number() over partition by job_id order by seq desc picks the last run)
body_fields.output: string, the run's output; the error is in its tail (last 2000 chars kept by evolve)

tsd.leases.id_format: 'cron/' + esc(esc(job_id) + '/' + str(occurrence_ms)), where esc replaces '%' with '%25' then '/' with '%2F' (tinyflows Key::of(["cron", Key::of([job_id, occurrence_ms])]); bin/lib/catch_up.py _lease_id)

body_fields.released: truthy when the claim was let go
body_fields.expires_ms: integer epoch ms; the lease is live while expires_ms > now
body_fields.holder: string, who holds the claim (compared before/after a re-arm)
body_fields.epoch: integer, the fence; a new acquisition changes holder and epoch

tsd.leases.rule: live = not released and expires_ms > now_ms and max(updated_ms, expires_ms - OCCURRENCE_LEASE_MS) >= now_ms - LEASE_FRESH_SECS*1000

notes: bin/seed-cron's rearm and health's stale_crons depend on next_run_ms and the tsd.leases claim being written by whatever runs the scheduler. If the TS core keeps a different scheduler store it must still write this table in this shape, or every one of these readers has to move with it.
